title: Coordinate Geometry: Gradient, Length and Equation of a Line
seo_title: Sec 3 Coordinate geometry Worksheets: Free Secondary 3 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: finding the gradient of a straight line given the coordinates of two points on it; finding the length of a line segment given the coordinates of its end points; interpreting and finding the equation of a straight line graph in the form y = mx + c; geometric problems involving the use of coordinates
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 maths worksheets on coordinate geometry: gradient from two points, length of a line segment, equations y = mx + c, parallel lines and geometric problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: In y = mx + c, m is the gradient and c is the y-intercept. Parallel lines have equal gradients.
body_html:
How it works

  • Gradient of the line through (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) = (y2 − y1) ÷ (x2 − x1).
  • Length = √((x2 − x1)2 + (y2 − y1)2). This is Pythagoras' theorem on the grid.
  • In y = mx + c, m is the gradient and c is the y-intercept. To find c, substitute a point on the line.
  • Parallel lines have equal gradients.
Example

Find the equation of the line through (1, 2) and (3, 8).

Gradient = (8 − 2) ÷ (3 − 1) = 3

2 = 3 × 1 + c, so c = −1

Answer: y = 3x − 1

Example

Find the length of the line joining (−1, 2) and (5, −6).

√(6² + (−8)²) = √(36 + 64) = √100

Answer: 10 units

Common mistakes

  • Working out run ÷ rise instead of rise ÷ run.
  • Subtracting the x-values in one order and the y-values in the other.
  • Forgetting the square root at the end of the length formula.
  • Mixing up the gradient and the y-intercept in 2y = 6x + 4. Divide by 2 first: y = 3x + 2.

faq.q: How do you find the gradient from two points?
faq.a: Divide the change in y by the change in x: (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁). Keep the points in the same order on top and bottom.

faq.q: How do you find the length of a line segment?
faq.a: Use √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²). It is Pythagoras' theorem with the horizontal and vertical distances as the shorter sides.

faq.q: How do you find the equation of a straight line?
faq.a: Find the gradient m, then substitute one point into y = mx + c to find c.

faq.q: How can I tell if two lines are parallel?
faq.a: Write both in the form y = mx + c. If the gradients m are equal, the lines are parallel.
